newsitem.title: USA: Clinton stretches lead over Dole in California.
newsitem.headline: Clinton stretches lead over Dole in California.

text.p: President Clinton has stretched his lead to 22 points over Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole in California, according to an opinion poll published Thursday.

The statewide poll by the independent Field Institute, conducted after last week's Democratic convention, found that Clinton's lead over Dole now stands at 55 percent to 33 percent among likely voters in the Nov. 5 election.

Clinton has regained the large lead he had over Dole prior to last month's Republican nominating convention, the poll found. In mid-August, immediately after the Republican convention, Dole had narrowed the gap to just 10 points in the state, with 35 per cent to Clinton's 45 percent.

The Field poll was carried out between Aug. 29 and Sept. 3 among a representative statewide sample of 825 registered voters, of whom 605 were deemed likely to vote in November. The overall sample had a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points, while the margin of error for the likely voter sample was 4.1 percent.

The poll was taken in the days after top Clinton political adviser Dick Morris resigned after a supermarket tabloid reported an alleged affair with a high-priced call girl. But the incident apparently had little impact on Californian.
Statewide, 81 percent of likely voters said the Morris affair would have no effect on how they will vote for president, the Field Institute said.

Support for the Reform Party's nominee, Texas billionaire Ross Perot, and the Green Party's Ralph Nader in California remained small, with Perot taking 4 percent and Nader polling 2 percent, the Field Institute found. Only 6 percent of the likely voters surveyed in the poll said they were undecided.

Sixty percent of the state's registered voters said they had a favourable view of Clinton, while just 38 percent said they have a favourable view of Dole. The image that voters have of Perot has become even more negative. At present, 70 percent of the state's voters hold a negative view of Perot.
California, with 54 electoral votes, is seen as essential to Clinton's re-election chances, which he has underscored with numerous visits to the state throughout his presidency.
